title: Virginia's 1st Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Virginia's 1st Congressional District stretches from the Northern Neck and Middle Peninsula down to the northern Richmond suburbs, including parts of Henrico, Chesterfield, Hanover, and James City counties. Incumbent Republican Rep. Rob Wittman, first elected in 2007, is seeking re-election in a district that backed Donald Trump by roughly five points in 2024 but also supported Democrat Abigail Spanberger for governor in 2025. A seven-candidate Democratic primary on August 4, 2026, will determine who challenges Wittman in the general election, with the contest rated as 'Lean Republican' by the Cook Political Report. Shannon Taylor, the Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney, leads the Democratic field in fundraising and has the most institutional endorsements, though the primary remains competitive.
polling_note: Only one publicly available poll was found, a PPP poll conducted for a Democratic group in August 2025 testing Wittman vs. Shannon Taylor.

candidates.name: Rob Wittman
candidates.summary: Rob Wittman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 1st Congressional District, first elected in a 2007 special election. He serves as Vice Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee and the House Natural Resources Committee, focusing on national defense, shipbuilding, the Chesapeake Bay, and rural broadband. Prior to Congress, he worked for 26 years at the Virginia Department of Health's Division of Shellfish Sanitation and served on the Montross Town Council and Westmoreland County Board of Supervisors.

candidates.name: Shannon Taylor
candidates.summary: Shannon Taylor is the Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney, first elected in 2011 and re-elected three times. She is the first woman and first Democrat in decades to hold the office. Taylor previously ran for Virginia Attorney General in 2025, losing in the Democratic primary. She has endorsements from Governor Abigail Spanberger, numerous state legislators, and EMILY's List, and has raised over $1.3 million for her congressional campaign. Her platform focuses on lowering costs, fighting corruption, and protecting healthcare access.

candidates.summary: Jason Knapp is a former U.S. Navy Commander and F/A-18 pilot who served for 21 years, including as a defense fellow assigned to the House Armed Services Committee and as Deputy Director of Legislative Affairs for U.S. European Command. He advocates for universal healthcare, reproductive freedom, and workers' rights. Knapp has raised over $500,000 for his campaign and emphasizes his experience in national security and bipartisan governance.

forecast.rationale: Incumbent Republican Rep. Rob Wittman, first elected in 2007, holds a meaningful advantage rooted in nearly two decades of incumbency, senior committee positions (Vice Chair of Armed Services and Natural Resources), and a district that backed Donald Trump by roughly five points in 2024 — both structural factors favoring the GOP. Cook Political Report rates the race 'Lean Republican,' aligning with this assessment. However, uncertainty is elevated by several factors: only one public poll exists (a Democratic-affiliated PPP survey from August 2025 showing Wittman at 41% vs. Shannon Taylor at 40%, essentially tied), the district also supported Democrat Abigail Spanberger for governor in 2025, and a seven-candidate Democratic primary on August 4, 2026, remains unresolved. Shannon Taylor leads in fundraising ($1.3M) and endorsements, but the eventual nominee is still unknown, introducing additional variability. With the election 4.5 months away and limited polling, the race is competitive but leans Republican.
